content: This combination medication, which includes acetaminophen, butalbital, and caffeine, is prescribed to alleviate tension headaches. It may also be used for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. This medication is available in capsule and tablet form and is taken orally. It is typically taken every four hours as needed. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take this medication exactly as directed. Do not exceed six tablets or capsules in a single day. If you feel that your symptoms are not adequately controlled, contact your doctor. Be aware that this medication has the potential to be habit-forming. Do not take a higher dose, take it more frequently, or use it for a longer duration than prescribed by your doctor. Before starting this medication, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to acetaminophen, butalbital, caffeine, or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), antidepressants, antihistamines, pain relievers, sedatives, sleeping aids, tranquilizers, and vitamins. Many over-the-counter pain relievers contain acetaminophen, and excessive amounts of this drug can be harmful. Notify your doctor if you have a history of liver disease, porphyria, or depression. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can exacerbate the drowsiness caused by this medication, so avoid consuming alcohol while taking it. This medication may cause stomach upset. To minimize this, take it with food or milk. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. This medication may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: drowsiness, upset stomach, vomiting, stomach pain, depression, lightheadedness, or confusion. If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: skin rash, itching, or difficulty breathing. Serious side effects should also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly; consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and any required laboratory tests. Your doctor may order tests to monitor your response to this medication. Do not share this medication with anyone else. This medication is a controlled substance, and refills may be limited. If you have questions about refills, consult your pharmacist. This medication is sold under various brand names, including Amaphen®, Anoquan®, Butace®, Endolor®, Esgic®, Fioricet®, Medigesic®, and Repan®.
